messages:
Ella: Hey team — Acero POC on hold. Customer reports rerank endpoint returning 400 with "embedding_dim_mismatch" and intermittent 429s when they send batched candidate vectors. Can eng swarm? :pray:
Raj: Got it. Can you share the exact request body and encoder version?
Ella: They sent two requests (trimmed):
POST /v1/models/redwood-embed-512/encode
{ "input": ["doc1","doc2"], "return_embeddings": true, "batch_size": 64 }
POST /v1/rerank
{ "query": "how to onboard", "candidates": [[...embedding vectors...]] }
They said their encoder returns 768-dim vectors but used redwood-embed-512 for rerank.
Marta: That explains the mismatch immediately — 768 != 512. Two paths: (A) they re-encode with the 512 checkpoint (recommended) or (B) run a projection 768->512 server-side as a temporary shim (approximate, not ideal long-term).
Kevin: 429s likely from their large batch_size and hitting per-request compute/time limits. Suggest lowering batch_size to 8-16 and implement exponential backoff. I'll check their tenant rate metrics.
Ella: Error body they saw:
{ "error": "embedding_dim_mismatch", "message": "expected embedding dim 512 but got 768" }
Raj: I'll DM the customer to switch encoder config. Meanwhile, can we make our rerank errors clearer? Add suggested dims in the response.
Marta: Quick mitigation: return an enriched error with an X-Embed-Dims header containing expected/got. We can also log a metric "dim_mismatch". Server-side projection would require product sign-off.
Kevin: Deployed a small change to staging to include dims header and clearer text. Also added metric for dim_mismatch. deploy-bot: Deploy queued: rerank-error-enhancements v2.3.1 to staging — started by @Kevin — ETA ~10m.
Ella: Customer asks about cost to re-encode ~2.5M docs. Any ballpark?
Raj: Rough estimate: re-encode cost = compute per-embedding * docs. I'll produce numbers in 24h. Recommend lazy re-encode: prioritize hot docs first.
Marta: We can offer a discounted reserved batch slot for the POC to speed re-encoding. Also point them to our batch-encoding job runner for cheaper throughput.
Ella: Security question: will server-side projection persist vectors outside tenant storage?
Kevin: No. Embeddings live in tenant blobstore. Any transient projection is in-memory only unless the customer asks us to persist results. We'll add a short security note for their questionnaire.
Ella: I'll send remediation checklist to the customer: 1) stop sending 768-d vectors to 512 model, 2) reduce batch_size to 8-16, 3) add retry/backoff, 4) consider re-encoding with correct encoder.
Raj: I'll draft how-to examples and a cost ballpark.
Marta: Follow-up internal action — add public doc about embedding-dim pitfalls and update developer quickstart to call out common encoder/model mismatches.
Ella: Thanks all — I'll update once customer tests fixes. :thumbsup:
